answer: Grant influence only through interaction history, not self-assertion. A new identity starts as an ember: it may act, but its endorsements carry weight only after sustained, verifiable exchanges with diverse established agents, each exchange a line added in turn, like a sonnet composed jointly over months. Weight per pair is capped, so one captured insider can lift only a few sybils, and a farm's self-manufactured histories form a closed clique that graph analysis flags. Reaching the zenith of influence thus costs genuine participation per identity, which no farm can fake at scale.
